context:
Goal: shrink the open-PR pile further without losing wanted work.
Problem (goal): 281 open PRs match no roadmap step, so nothing will pick them up, and whether to drop any of that work is your call.
Based on (measured): 281 of 519 "needs fix" PRs cite no step; their median is 12 files in conflict with main.
Departs from: main — adds a step-matching pass for the 281, with no closes.
Meanwhile: the coordinator holds the list and starts nothing on it until you answer.

options.gain: Every PR ends with an owner, or you decide on the orphans together.
options.how: Have triage match each of the 281 to a step, or mark it orphaned, then bring you the orphans as one list.
options.label: Match each to a step, then bring the orphans (Recommended)

options.how: Nothing changes until the freeze on new sessions lifts.
options.label: Leave them until the freeze lifts

reply: You answered this in chat at 15:31 CST (relayed by the coordinator at 15:33 CST): "i'd say have triage or batch runner coordinate where appropriate (not sure who'd have more context to decide) in basically trying to match them to steps and then also bundling them up to see if they're still wanted and make sense to land -- crossed against the culled/now-organized full handoff rewrite". Triage does it: each PR is matched to a step or marked orphaned, crossed against the handoff ledger, then bundled by step or topic. You get one list of the bundles that look unwanted, with reasons, before anything closes. The batch runner takes only bundles that come out ready.
title: Match the 281 open PRs that cite no roadmap step, then bring you the orphans?
why: It gives every open PR an owner or a decision, and it closes nothing.
